title: Rename usage module and use Nexus auth
description: The bundled usage code still carries the old pi-slash-usage name and reads auth from ~/.pi/agent/auth.json. Rename the source module to slash-usage and make provider token readers use Nexus auth storage only.
acceptance_criteria: Source imports use src/slash-usage, usage auth reads Nexus agent auth via Nexus config resolution, legacy ~/.pi auth is no longer used by the usage module, and regression tests cover the auth path.
notes: Renamed src/pi-slash-usage to src/slash-usage, updated neo-editor usage imports, removed stale release staging script for external pi-slash-usage, and replaced readPiAuth with readNexusAuth that reads NEXUS_CODING_AGENT_DIR or ~/.local/share/nexus/agent only. Validation: npx tsx --test test/slash-usage/readNexusAuth.test.ts test/slash-usage/selectUsagePair.test.ts test/extensions/fff/handleInternalModelCommand.test.ts test/extensions/fff/ensureEnabledModelIncludesSelection.test.ts.
close_reason: Implemented rename and Nexus-only auth path.

title: Fix Nexus scoped model persistence dropping new models
description: Nexus custom slash scoped-model save can persist an enabledModels allow-list that omits newly available models such as openai-codex/gpt-5.5. This causes startup and Ctrl+L model cycling/listing to filter those models even though /models and --list-models can see them. Fix the Nexus-owned save behavior and add regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Saving scoped models through the Nexus internal command preserves newly available/unseen models already absent from the picker state unless explicitly disabled, and tests cover the regression.
notes: Implemented Nexus model selection persistence fix by appending a selected model to enabledModels when a scoped allow-list already exists. Also fixed Codex usage matching so gpt-5.5 no longer matches gpt-5.3 Spark windows. Validation: targeted tsx tests pass; full npm test timed out at 120s and 300s; npx tsc --noEmit still fails on pre-existing project-wide type errors.
close_reason: Fixed in source with regression tests.

title: Refresh promptline cache before startup resume auto-submit
description: Running just dev --resume can leave the startup resume selector stuck with a raw /nexus-resume-select payload in the editor. The startup resume flow writes a new exact-match submit trigger, but the Neo promptline keeps the trigger config cached from session_start and does not reload it before ctx.ui.setEditorText() runs. First-time resume selections therefore fail to auto-submit until the identical trigger already exists on disk. Refresh the cached promptline config before priming the internal resume command, and add a deterministic regression test that covers selector choice -> primed submit.
notes:
Validation:
- npx tsx --test test/extensions/neo-editor/slashCommandSubmit.test.ts test/extensions/neo-editor/promptlineEditorConfigCache.test.ts test/extensions/neo-editor/startupResumeSubmit.test.ts test/runtime/cli/getCurrentNexusLaunchSpec.test.ts

Fix:
- refresh the cached promptline config after writing the startup resume submit trigger and before ctx.ui.setEditorText()
- added a regression test that exercises the startup resume selector through PromptlineEditor cached-config state
close_reason: Refreshed the cached promptline config before priming the startup resume command and added a regression test that proves the selector path auto-submits through PromptlineEditor.

title: Eliminate idle polling in sub-agent status widget
description: The sub-agent status widget currently starts a 100ms session-long interval on session_start and repeatedly calls ctx.ui.setWidget() even when no foreground or background work is active. This causes high idle CPU, especially after resuming a session. Replace the polling path with Pi's built-in working-indicator animation for foreground work, keep the async widget event-driven, and add regression tests so idle sessions do not install a polling redraw loop.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix Telegram adapter RPC timeout replay loop
description:
## Summary
Telegram adapter can enter a replay loop after an RPC prompt timeout because the child session remains busy and the polling offset is only persisted after a full successful batch.

## Why
Users receive repeated "Agent is already processing" failures from Telegram and cannot stop the loop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- timeouted Telegram RPC prompts reset the stuck chat session
- Telegram polling persists progress per update so one bad message does not replay the whole batch
- regression tests cover timeout recovery and per-update offset persistence
close_reason: Closed

title: Add regression coverage for lazy FFF startup behavior
description:
Why: This startup regression happened because FFF initialization behavior was not locked down by tests. We need deterministic coverage that proves Nexus does not initialize FFF during startup and still initializes it correctly on first use.

What: Add focused regression tests for the bundled FFF extension lifecycle and first-use paths, including startup without FileFinder creation and on-demand initialization from an FFF-backed entrypoint. Prefer deterministic source-mode tests and add e2e coverage if the startup path needs full-app verification.
acceptance_criteria: tests fail if FFF initializes during startup again and pass when first-use lazy initialization still works
notes:
Validation:
- npx tsx --test test/extensions/fff/registerFffExtension.test.ts test/extensions/fff/createFffAutocompleteProvider.test.ts
- Added registerFffExtension lifecycle regression coverage plus autocomplete fallback coverage.
close_reason: Added deterministic regression coverage for lazy startup lifecycle, lazy tool initialization, first-use failure reporting, and autocomplete fallback behavior.

title: Ensure @ autocomplete, read, and grep trigger FFF lazily
description:
Why: After removing eager startup initialization, all FFF-backed entrypoints must still work when the runtime has not been initialized yet. The first actual @ autocomplete, read override, or grep override call must create the finder on demand and surface failures in the right place.

What: Verify and adjust the FFF-backed editor and tool entrypoints so they call ensure only when needed, keep fallback behavior correct, and avoid startup-only warnings for failures that now belong to first use.
acceptance_criteria: @ autocomplete, FFF-backed read, and FFF-backed grep still work after lazy init; failures are reported on first relevant use instead of at startup
close_reason: FFF-backed read, grep, and @ autocomplete now rely on first-use initialization; autocomplete falls back cleanly on init failure and first-use warnings are emitted instead of startup warnings.

title: Stop eager FFF initialization during session_start
description:
Why: src/extensions/fff/registerFffExtension.ts currently awaits activeRuntime.ensure() on every session_start, which defeats lazy loading and forces the native FFF indexer to run at launch.

What: Refactor the FFF extension lifecycle so session_start creates and stores a lightweight FffRuntime only. Remove the eager ensure call, keep disposal behavior correct across session switches, and ensure no startup path triggers FileFinder creation before first FFF use.
acceptance_criteria: session_start no longer initializes FileFinder; runtime store/disposal still works correctly across session start/shutdown
close_reason: session_start now installs a lightweight FffRuntime without awaiting ensure, and lifecycle regression coverage confirms runtime store/disposal still works.

title: Lazy-load FFF runtime to eliminate Nexus startup CPU spikes
description:
Why: Nexus eagerly calls FFF runtime initialization during session_start, which creates the native FileFinder and kicks off indexing before the user or model has requested any FFF-backed behavior. That makes every Nexus launch pay the FFF startup cost even when @ autocomplete, FFF-backed read, and FFF-backed grep are never used.

What: Change the bundled FFF integration so session startup only installs lightweight runtime state, while native FileFinder creation happens on first real FFF use. Keep feature behavior intact for @ autocomplete and the FFF-backed read/grep paths, add regression coverage, and capture before/after startup evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Nexus startup with FFF enabled no longer creates the native FileFinder during session_start; FFF still initializes on first real use; regression coverage and startup-profile evidence are attached
close_reason: Lazy FFF initialization is implemented, regression-tested, and backed by interactive startup evidence showing lightweight fff session_start work.

title: Remove extra empty spacing around Tron thinking blocks
description: Why: Tron currently renders extra empty spacing above and below assistant thinking blocks, which makes the compact transcript feel loose and inconsistent with the intended tight layout.\n\nWhat: Inspect the Tron thinking renderer and spacing patches, remove the unwanted blank spacing above and below thinking while preserving tool adjacency and message readability, add or update deterministic regression coverage, and verify the targeted tests.

title: Reduce keystroke handling to in-memory slash and @ logic
description: Why: During typing, the editor should only react to the special cases that affect live UI behavior: slash as the first character in the prompt and @ for file selection.\n\nWhat: Refactor handleInput()/trigger flow so per-keystroke work is synchronous and in memory, limited to slash-first-character detection, @ trigger handling, modal routing, and normal editor updates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Refresh cached promptline config only on reload
description: Why: Cached trigger and Neo settings still need a supported refresh path when the user explicitly reloads.\n\nWhat: Define reload semantics for promptline config, update the cached trigger/settings state on reload, and ensure normal typing does not invalidate or re-read config.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cache editor trigger config at session startup
description: Why: Trigger config should not be read from disk on every keystroke. It should be available in memory for the whole session.\n\nWhat: Load merged editor trigger config once during session startup, store it in promptline/editor state, and have keystroke handling consult the cached value instead of calling readEditorTriggerConfig() during input.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cache Neo editor settings at session startup
description: Why: Neo settings like clearEditorOnTriggerSubmit do not need per-keystroke disk reads.\n\nWhat: Load Neo config once during session startup, keep it in memory for the session, and remove readNeoConfig() from the hot typing path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit Neo editor keystroke path and document async work
description: Why: We need an exact inventory of what currently runs on each keystroke before changing behavior.\n\nWhat: Trace the Neo editor input path, identify every async call, file read, modal refresh, and render request triggered during typing, and capture the expected minimal behavior for slash-at-first-character and @ file selection.

title: Eliminate per-keystroke Neo editor config I/O
description: Why: The custom Neo/Tron editor currently performs async config and trigger work during typing. Trigger rules and Neo settings should be loaded once at startup and refreshed only on explicit reload, while per-keystroke handling should stay in memory and react only to prompt semantics like leading slash and @ file selection.\n\nWhat: Remove per-keystroke config reads from the editor input path, cache trigger/settings state at startup, refresh that cache on reload, constrain live input handling to the minimum needed for slash-first-character and @ file selection, and add profiling/regression coverage.

title: Reintegrate Tron grouping reconstruction removed in stash
description: Restore the recently removed Tron assistant/tool grouping reconstruction logic from the stash so grouped thinking/tool presentation works again. Reintegrate only the relevant Tron activity and thinking bridge changes, add regression coverage, and verify behavior.

title: Restore stashed feature-flag work while preserving dev-profile
description: Why: Multiple git stashes contain relevant feature-flag and runtime work that must be restored without losing the dev-profile startup comparison flow.\n\nWhat: Reapply the stash contents needed onto the current branch, resolve conflicts, and verify just dev-profile still compares baseline vs --no-extensions startup profiling.

title: Add regression tests for source-vs-release flag behavior
description: Why: This bug happened because source and release feature-flag behavior drifted apart without test coverage that enforced the boundary.\n\nWhat: Add or split tests to prove source mode reads root feature-flags.json directly, release mode reads compiled flags, compiled bundled extension ids match generated release inputs, and toggling root JSON in source mode changes enabled extensions without regeneration.

title: Make just release regenerate and consume compiled flag artifacts
description: Why: Release builds must still compile only the enabled feature set, but that should happen at release build time from the current root JSON file.\n\nWhat: Verify and, if needed, tighten the release/build pipeline so just release regenerates compiledFeatureFlags and registerCompiledEnabledExtensions from feature-flags.json before bundling, with no stale artifact path left in source mode.

title: Confine compiled feature flags to release-only code paths
description: Why: Generated compiled flags should only be used by compiled release execution. Right now those generated artifacts leak into source mode and become the effective runtime config.\n\nWhat: Refactor feature-flag access boundaries so source/dev paths use root JSON, while release/bundled paths continue using getBundledFeatureFlagsConfig() and compiled artifacts only.

title: Make feature-flags.json the source of truth
description: Why: Source/dev runs currently ignore the root feature-flags.json file and instead read stale generated compiled flags, causing disabled extensions like tron to stay active until generated artifacts are refreshed. We need one clear source of truth for development while preserving compile-time feature selection for release builds.\n\nWhat: Make root feature-flags.json the runtime source of truth for source/dev runs, keep compiled feature flags and compiled bundled extension selection as release-only artifacts generated during just release, and add regression coverage so source and release behavior cannot drift again.

title: Switch source runtime feature flags to root JSON
description: Why: readFeatureFlagsConfig() currently returns compiledFeatureFlags for source runs, which makes development ignore feature-flags.json changes.\n\nWhat: Update the source runtime feature-flag read path so dev/source runs load feature-flags.json from disk via the JSON reader, and verify createExtensionFeatureFlags() respects that config immediately without regenerating compiled artifacts.

title: Disable heavy startup extensions except tron
description: Why: Startup profiling showed a CPU spike dominated by a heavy set of bundled extensions. The requested change is to disable the heavy startup contributors while keeping tron enabled.\n\nWhat: Update the bundled feature flags so fff, neo-editor, observations, sub-agents, and todo are disabled, keep tron enabled, regenerate any compiled feature-flag artifacts needed for release parity, and validate the relevant tests/profile command.
close_reason: Closed

title: Isolate startup CPU extension culprit
description: Why: We confirmed startup CPU drops when --no-extensions is passed, so we need to identify which bundled extension or combination causes the startup spike.\n\nWhat: Run a controlled extension-isolation search in dev mode, enabling subsets and individual extensions, capture startup-profile artifacts, and report the extension(s) responsible for the CPU spike.
close_reason: Closed

description: Why: Nexus currently passes --no-extensions through to Pi only, while still loading its own bundled extensions. Users expect the same CLI flag to disable all extensions consistently.\n\nWhat: Update Nexus startup so a user-supplied --no-extensions or -ne also disables bundled extension factories, remove reliance on NEXUS_DISABLE_BUNDLED_EXTENSIONS for normal CLI behavior, and add regression tests covering dev/release startup paths.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement Nexus parity for built-in Pi selector slash menus
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The custom Nexus slash UI still falls through to Pi for several built-in slash commands that open selector-style interactive menus. We need explicit parity tasks for each built-in slash command that launches a selector or submenu flow in Pi interactive mode, so Nexus can keep the full interaction inside the custom UI.

Source: node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js

Included selector-style commands:
- /settings -> showSettingsSelector()
- /scoped-models -> showModelsSelector()
- /model -> handleModelCommand() / showModelSelector()
- /fork -> showUserMessageSelector()
- /tree -> showTreeSelector() with branch-summary follow-up selector
- /resume -> showSessionSelector()
- /login -> showOAuthSelector("login")
- /logout -> showOAuthSelector("logout")

Goal:
- keep these flows inside the custom Nexus slash UI
- stop handing them off to Pi builtin selectors
- add parity coverage for each flow
acceptance_criteria: Every built-in Pi slash command that opens a selector-style interactive menu is tracked as a child issue and implemented inside the Nexus custom slash UI without falling through to Pi builtin selectors
close_reason: Closed

title: Add regression coverage for the Pi-runtime-backed Nexus settings menu

title: Map Nexus settings actions to Pi-equivalent runtime behavior only
description:

Work:
- implement write/apply behavior per Pi runtime settings callbacks
- ensure theme, thinking, image, transport, and UI settings behave like Pi
- route model/provider handling out of the settings menu
acceptance_criteria: Every visible Nexus settings item applies the same behavior category Pi uses; non-settings flows like model/provider are not handled in the settings submenu

title: Read Pi runtime settings-selector config for visible settings items and options

- preserve Pi ordering and submenu shape

title: Remove generic merged-settings editing from the Nexus slash menu
description:

The current settings branch builds leaves from Object.entries of merged settings and treats non-boolean values as pseudo-editable items. That behavior is incorrect and must be removed.

Work:

acceptance_criteria: The settings menu no longer uses raw merged settings as the editable source; items like defaultModel/defaultProvider no longer appear as editable settings entries

title: Rewrite Nexus settings menu to use Pi runtime settings selector contract only
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The current Nexus slash settings menu incorrectly treats merged JSON settings as a generic editable schema. That diverges from Pi. We need to remove that behavior and rebuild the Nexus settings menu so it derives items, values, and submenu options from Pi runtime settings-selector behavior only, with no fallback path and no compatibility layer.

Scope:
- remove the raw merged-settings-as-editor approach
- read the live Pi settings selector contract at runtime
- show only the settings Pi /settings actually exposes
- use the exact Pi-backed values and option lists for those items
- route non-settings behavior like model/provider selection out of this menu
- add regression tests for the Pi-runtime-backed settings menu contract

Non-goals:
- do not keep the old generic settings editor path
- do not add compatibility fallbacks for older Pi contracts
- do not keep settings entries that Pi does not expose in /settings
acceptance_criteria: Nexus settings menu is derived only from Pi runtime settings-selector behavior; non-Pi settings entries are removed; submenu options match Pi runtime values; tests lock the runtime-backed contract

title: Unify Neo trigger controller for @ and / overlays
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The Neo editor currently has partially unified trigger behavior for @ and /, but their live input-routing and modal lifecycle still differ. This causes regressions like slash reopening unexpectedly, paste-path false positives, and inconsistent cancel/reopen behavior between triggers.

This issue tracks the remaining work to create one generic trigger controller in Neo that owns trigger session lifecycle, modal launch, cancellation, invalidation, and input routing for @, /, and future trigger prefixes like #. Trigger-specific code should be limited to modal content/providers only.

Scope:
- build one generic trigger-session controller for Neo
- make @ and / use the exact same behavior path
- preserve FFF-backed @ content and slash-menu content as pluggable providers
- cover typed-start, cancel, paste, reopen, and invalidation cases with deterministic e2e tests

Non-goals:
- do not redesign modal visuals beyond what is needed for behavior parity
- do not expand settings/features unrelated to trigger behavior
- do not add new trigger prefixes yet; only leave the controller ready for them
design: Keep behavior in Neo modules, not content-specific branches. The generic controller should manage typed trigger start, active-session tracking, input routing, close semantics, invalidation on text changes, and overlay reuse. Trigger-specific providers should only supply query parsing, item loading, preview content, and completion application.
acceptance_criteria: One generic trigger controller owns @ and / session lifecycle; @ and / differ only by provider/content; pasted paths or image OCR text must not auto-open slash UI; cancel with Ctrl+C/Esc must fully clear the active trigger session; deterministic virtual-terminal e2e coverage proves parity for @ and / behavior

title: Add CLI session listing and direct resume-by-id

What: add a discoverable CLI option to list available sessions from the executable itself and allow 'nexus --resume <session-id>' to resolve directly into that session while preserving the custom picker for bare --resume. Include deterministic regression coverage for both commands in the virtual-terminal harness.
acceptance_criteria: 'nexus --sessions' prints resumable session identifiers from the CLI. 'nexus --resume <session-id>' starts directly in the requested session. Bare '--resume' still opens the Nexus picker. Deterministic tests cover the listing and direct-resume flows.
notes: Fixed source CLI session commands. npm/just dev now forwards flags through tsx using 'tsx -- src/index.ts'; runCliWithApp handles --sessions with the Nexus agent dir; direct --resume <session-id> rewrites to --session while bare --resume still opens the Nexus picker. Added source CLI and npm-run regression tests for sessions listing and direct resume.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add regression tests and typing-profile validation for Neo editor input
description: Why: We need coverage that locks in the new hot-path behavior and prevents config I/O from creeping back into typing.\n\nWhat: Add targeted tests for cached trigger/settings behavior, reload refresh behavior, slash-first-character handling, @ selection handling, and a profiling/diagnostic validation path showing reduced typing-time CPU.
close_reason: Closed

title: Debounce or eliminate redundant render churn in promptline typing
description: Why: Even after removing config I/O, unnecessary modal refreshes and requestRender calls can still amplify CPU usage while typing.\n\nWhat: Identify redundant render requests in promptline/trigger handling, remove or coalesce them, and keep visible behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Validate extension disabling and startup profiling end to end
description: Why: The user-facing symptom is that disabling extensions in feature-flags.json was not respected, and startup CPU behavior depended on stale generated flags.\n\nWhat: Run targeted validation showing a source run follows feature-flags.json immediately, release follows regenerated compiled artifacts after just release, and startup profiling reflects the enabled extension set in each mode.

title: Remove obsolete feature-flag mode helpers and stale assumptions
description: Why: Helpers and comments that imply compiled flags may be used broadly in runtime make the architecture harder to understand and easier to regress.\n\nWhat: Remove or simplify no-longer-needed mode helpers such as useCompiledFeatureFlags if they become dead code, and update docs/comments so the runtime truth boundary is explicit.

title: Update dev-profile startup confirmation
description: Why: We need a reproducible way to confirm the dev-only startup CPU spike comes from Nexus eager module loading rather than enabled extension registration.\n\nWhat: Update the just dev-profile recipe to run the same dev startup path twice with startup profiling enabled, once normally and once with NEXUS_DISABLE_BUNDLED_EXTENSIONS=1, then print the resulting profile log paths and guidance for comparing them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enable all bundled feature flags
description: Why: the app should ship with every bundled extension feature flag turned on in the root feature flag registry and compiled runtime config. What: update feature-flags.json, regenerate compiled feature flags, and verify the feature-flag tests still pass.
acceptance_criteria: All entries in feature-flags.json are enabled, compiled feature flags match the root config, and test/feature-flags/featureFlags.test.ts passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace dev-profile with session CPU profiler
description: Why: the current dev-profile recipe samples a short-lived child tree and fails because just dev detaches the target process. What: replace it with a recipe that launches the Nexus dev app under Node CPU profiling for the full interactive session, then prints where the CPU profile artifacts were written after the process exits; keep help text aligned.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add dev-profile just recipe
description: Why: developers need a one-command way to profile CPU hotspots in the local Nexus dev process and inspect the sampled stacks. What: add a development just recipe that launches just dev, locates the target process, captures a macOS sample profile, and prints where the output is stored; update command help accordingly.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bring justfiles into compliance with justfile rules
description: Audit the root justfile and imported recipe files against the project justfile skill. Fix rule violations such as multiple recipes per file and keep the help/import structure aligned with the modular justfile conventions.
acceptance_criteria: Root justfile remains modular and each recipe lives in its own matching justfiles/*.just file
notes: Audited root justfile imports and recipe files against the justfile skill. The main rule violation was multiple recipes in justfiles/building/release.just. Split pub and pub-full into their own matching files and updated the root justfile imports. Verified the modular justfile still parses via 'just help'.
close_reason: Each root recipe now lives in its own matching justfiles/*.just file and the root justfile imports remain modular.

title: Show relative age in resume modal session list
description: In the Nexus resume modal, session timestamps should render as compact relative ages like 3m, 2h, or 5d instead of locale date strings. Implement with regression coverage.
notes: Resume rows now show compact summary metadata in the order human, tool, thinking, time. Implemented via src/extensions/shared/slash-menu/readResumeSessionStats.ts, formatResumeSummary.ts, and formatResumeAge.ts, with regression coverage in test/extensions/fff/createResumeLeavesSummary.test.ts.
close_reason: Resume list now uses compact relative summary metadata with counts and time.
